acquiesce

ak-wee-ESS · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To acquiesce is to accept without protest.

After a long, exhausting debate, the tired committee members finally chose to acquiesce to the chairman's proposal.

Worked Example

Rather than fight the new dress code any longer, most of the staff simply acquiesced.

Giving up resistance and going along with a rule you didn't originally agree with, without a fight, is exactly what acquiesce describes.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

comply: To comply is to actively do what a rule or request asks -- fill out the form, wear the badge. To acquiesce is quieter: you stop objecting and let something happen, without necessarily doing anything yourself. Comply is about action; acquiesce is about giving up resistance.

yield: To yield is to give way under visible pressure -- you were pushed, and you bent. To acquiesce is more passive still: you simply stop protesting and accept the situation, sometimes with no one pushing at all. Yield spotlights the pressure; acquiesce spotlights the silence.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

resist: refuse to accept or comply with

defy: openly refuse to obey

Where it sits · how deeply the will gives way — agree → acquiesce → submit

agree vs. acquiesce: To agree is simply to share an opinion; to acquiesce is to give up resistance and go along, often reluctantly.

submit vs. acquiesce: Submit can imply an even deeper surrender of will than acquiesce, sometimes to a person or authority rather than just a single decision.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ac-

prefix — ac-: toward (Latin (ad-))

root — quiesc

root — quiesc: to rest, be quiet (Latin (quiescere))

suffix — -e

suffix — -e: verb-forming ending (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Ac- ('toward') plus quiesc- ('to rest, be quiet') gives 'to settle into rest' -- to acquiesce is to stop resisting and quietly go along.

Use the root in a new word: quiescent

Use the root in a new word: quiescent: Quiescent ('inactive, dormant') shares the same quiescere root as acquiesce -- both are about settling into stillness rather than resisting.

Root Check

Word Choice

Acquiesce almost always carries a note of reluctance -- giving up a fight you didn't necessarily want to give up. Compare "accede" (this same unit), which is a more plain, formal word for agreeing to a specific demand or request.
